q.q: Round Robin scheduling assigns the CPU to each process for a fixed time slice. This policy is best described as:
q.x: Round Robin is preemptive: a process runs for one time quantum and is then preempted and placed at the back of the ready queue.

q.q: Which scheduling algorithm is known to give the minimum average waiting time (among non-preemptive algorithms)?
q.x: SJF is provably optimal for minimum average waiting time among non-preemptive policies, but it requires knowledge of burst times.

q.q: In Round Robin scheduling, if the time quantum is made very large, the behaviour becomes similar to which algorithm?
q.x: A large quantum means each process effectively runs to completion in arrival order, so Round Robin degrades to FCFS.

q.q: Which CPU scheduling algorithm is non-preemptive and executes processes in the order they arrive?
q.x: First Come First Served (FCFS) schedules in arrival order and is non-preemptive. It can suffer from the convoy effect.
